Q: Unity crashes after I run my save file script A:

As mentioned this is a combination of various things

  • First of all it makes no sense to try and plain out serialize a GameObject to JSON.

    look alone at GameObject.transform <-> Transform.gameObject and GameObject has a ton of such properties that can go very deep nested loops. it also has legacy properties like e.g. renderer, camera, collider, rigidbody etc. They are obsolete but exist

    you are basically trying to force it to serialize entire prefab code just worse.

    Anyway, what exactly is a GameObject supposed to look like in JSON? I'm pretty sure this is not what you want at all.

    What you can do is e.g. check for attached components, have a deep serialization and later when loading that save again create them one by one. Not sure if this is what you really want and need here.

    To me it sounds like some sort of "serialize all balls of certain type" thing to me. So the solution here would be simply store just that type and when loading create them accordingly.

  • and then it is known that Vector3 doesn't really play well with Newtonsoft JSON because it contains some properties which again return Vector themselves (e.g. normalized) and Newtonsoft tries to serialize them all basically ending in an infinite serialization loop. You ignored those but then there are also other properties which return float and you will still serialize them (magnitude etc)

    For this you usually introduce your own custom mirror type which only is a plain x,y,z without any further fancyness and girth and back convert between them for the serialization.

Besides these

  • when using Rigidbody you can just use its position directly
  • when going through Transform then there is no reason to use GetComponent to get it

but that's rather minor side notes compared to the above

Q: Is it possible to make aref operator work with custom class in Common Lisp? A:

Like an ordinary macro, you need to generate code that tests the run-time value of array. Your code is testing the compile-time value, which will be the symbol arr.

(sb-ext:without-package-locks
  (define-compiler-macro aref (array &rest subscripts)
    `(typecase ,array
       (mystring
         (cl:aref (mystring-data ,array) ,@subscripts))
       (otherwise
         (cl:aref ,array ,@subscripts)))))

If there are type declarations in the environment, the compiler should be able to use them to optimize typecase.

Q: How to mask SSH private key on GitLab CI? A:

Encode with base64 and use redirection.

Store your variable base64 encoded.

Redirect it to ssh-add after decoding.

- ssh-add - < <(base64 -d "$SENTINEL_DB_RESET_SSH_KEY")
